summary: Broad human pancreas coverage is plausible, but targeted refinements are needed for merged mural cells, missing mesothelial/capsular cells, ductal substructure, and weak rare endocrine semantics.

issues.description: Pericytes and vascular smooth muscle are collapsed into one mural axis/module despite being distinct normal pancreatic vascular support populations.
issues.suggested_fix: Split into separate pericyte and vascular smooth muscle modules/axes, or add a gated/contrast refinement axis within the mural compartment.

issues.description: Mesothelial/capsular surface cells are not represented, although all-cell human pancreas preparations can contain this population.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a mesothelial module and plain axis using markers such as MSLN, WT1, UPK3B, KRT19, KRT8, KRT18, and/or PDPN as appropriate.

issues.description: Ductal cells are mostly represented by one broad identity plus a centroacinar/terminal duct refinement, missing useful normal ductal heterogeneity such as ion/fluid transport versus mucin/SPP1-high ductal programs.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a ductal refinement axis for bicarbonate/ion-transport ducts versus mucin or SPP1/KRT17-high ductal states, or sharpen the existing ductal modules accordingly.

issues.description: A separate pancreatic enterochromaffin/serotonin endocrine cell axis is over-specific for baseline human pancreas and risks importing a gut enterochromaffin identity rather than a canonical pancreatic cell type.
issues.suggested_fix: Recast this as a rare endocrine serotonergic state, keep it lower priority, or fold it into a broader rare endocrine-state axis with careful endocrine sibling negatives.

issues.description: The epsilon/ghrelin module includes weak or shared markers such as MLN, IAPP, SCG2, and PAX6; IAPP is strongly beta-associated and broad endocrine genes reduce specificity.
issues.suggested_fix: Strengthen the module around ghrelin-cell markers and remove or downweight beta/common endocrine genes, especially IAPP.

issues.description: The module name implies B/plasma coverage, but the marker set is conventional B-cell identity while plasma cells are already represented separately.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename or reinterpret this as a B-cell module/axis and keep plasma_cell as the antibody-secreting cell module.

out_of_scope: The global cycling, interferon, immediate-early stress, and ER-load axes are reasonable generic state axes for dissociation and secretory tissue context.
The 32-axis dimensionality is somewhat high but defensible for an all-cell human pancreas embedding with immune and stromal subtyping.
